leads.name: Golden Weeping Ash (Guldhængeask), Landbohøjskolens Have
leads.location_hint: South Garden (Sydhaven), facing Bülowsvej, Landbohøjskolens Have, Frederiksberg
leads.reason: Single-sourced: only kub.ku.dk's 2008 historical feature ('De gamle traeer i fakultetets have') describes it, ~150 years old at time of writing (so ~168 now), 4 m tall. No independent second source found for age or survival, and no other outlet mentions it by name. Also modest and unspectacular in stature ('despite modest size, has endured'), so it may not clear the visually-spectacular/historically-significant bar even if a second source turns up. Worth a direct query to the garden.

leads.name: Silver Linden double tree, Landbohøjskolens Have
leads.species: Silver Linden (Tilia tomentosa), planted as a pair grown together
leads.location_hint: just inside the garden from Flisehaven, Landbohøjskolens Have, Frederiksberg
leads.reason: Only the same single kub.ku.dk 2008 article describes it; no age given, no second source, no coordinates beyond a vague garden-internal reference.

leads.name: Zelkova group (4 trees grown together), Landbohøjskolens Have
leads.reason: Same single source, described as 'fragile'; also a multi-trunk cluster rather than one collectible point, and no age or health status beyond 'fragile' found.

leads.name: Wingnut (vingevalnød / Pterocarya) at Allégade, Frederiksberg
leads.location_hint: park area near Allégade, Frederiksberg (exact spot not found)
leads.reason: Cited by frederiksberg.dk-linked search summaries as 'approximately 200 years old, one of the municipality's oldest trees' but the source page that stated this could not be located directly (404 on the most likely URL); no second independent source, no coordinates, no confirmation the tree still stands. Needs a fresh search for the current frederiksberg.dk page or a call to the municipality's tree register.

leads.name: Lindens of Frederiksberg Slot garden
leads.reason: Described in passing by search summaries as 'the state's 300-year-old linden trees at Frederiksberg Slot', Denmark's oldest trees on Frederiksberg, but no primary source found describing them individually. Access is a real problem: the palace now houses the Army Officers' School (Haerens Officerskole) and is open for guided tours only about ten days a year (last Saturday of the month, per migogkbh.dk), so even if verified this would ship as 'restricted' access at best, not a casual walk-up. Needs a Slots- og Kulturstyrelsen or Forsvaret source with real detail before pursuing further.

leads.name: Giant plane tree, Assistens Kirkegaard
leads.species: London Plane or Oriental Plane (Platanus sp., not confirmed)
leads.location_hint: on a lawn somewhere in Assistens Kirkegaard, Norrebro
leads.reason: Multiple thin search-summary mentions of 'a preserved giant plane tree, possibly Denmark's largest' at Assistens Kirkegaard, also referenced as having 'iconic tree' status under Copenhagen's tree designation programme, but every page actually fetched this pass (kk.dk cemetery page, storyhunt.io guide) turned out to contain no tree detail at all when read directly, only the search engine's own AI summary asserted it. This is a real, promising lead (the cemetery is 500m-1km from the existing Botanisk Have/Kongens Have cluster, and holds Andersen's and Kierkegaard's graves) but needs a primary source located and fetched directly, not just a search summary, before verification. Do not treat the 'possibly Denmark's largest' claim as sourced; it was never traced to an origin this pass.

leads.name: Kastellet ramparts trees (elm, linden, horse chestnut)
leads.species: mixed: elm, linden, horse chestnut, various fruit trees
leads.location_hint: the star-shaped rampart of Kastellet, Copenhagen
leads.reason: Well documented that Kastellet's ramparts were deliberately planted with these species from 1663 onward (root systems to bind the earthworks, timber reserve, sightline-blocking), per fredninger.dk and hovedstadshistorie.dk, and the fortification itself is intact and highly walkable, directly adjacent to the existing Kongens Have/Botanisk Have cluster. But this is a planting programme across an entire rampart, not one identifiable tree, so no single specimen could be pulled out from what this pass read. Needs either a specific named/measured veteran tree (a Danish Dendrological Society register entry, as with Thorvaldsen's Robinia, would solve this in one fetch) or a site visit/photo survey to pick one out.
leads.note_for_ensemble_test: Even at its best this is closer to 'a fortification planted with trees' than one collectible point; would need one genuinely standout specimen, not the rampart as a whole.

leads.name: Copenhagen 'evighedstraeer' (eternity trees) designation
leads.species: unspecified, designated per-tree by the municipality
leads.location_hint: municipal nature areas only, e.g. Utterslev Mose; not city parks or gardens
leads.reason: Real, verified municipal programme (Koebenhavns Kommune Traepolitik, adopted 2016; criteria PDF read this pass: tree must be over 100 years old, beech >150, oak >200, diameter >1m, or carry major biological/historic/aesthetic value; ~50 eternity trees expected citywide) but the source material found is policy and committee minutes, not a published list of the actual designated trees with names or coordinates. Also structurally off the city's core walkable cluster: eternity trees are designated ONLY in municipal nature areas (Utterslev Mose, Amager Faelled, Vestvolden etc.), which sit well outside the Kongens Have/Botanisk Have/Slotsholmen spine and would need their own day-trip framing per the 30-minute rule. Needs the municipality's actual GIS layer or published tree list, not the policy document, before this goes anywhere.

blocked.name: Blodbøg (blood/copper beech), Landbohøjskolens Have
blocked.reason: CONFIRMED DEAD. Planted 1858 when the garden was founded (its oldest tree, 5 m circumference, described by fredninger.dk's older snapshot as the garden's thickest tree), but Danish Wikipedia's Landbohojskolens Have entry states plainly it 'blev faeldet i 2018 grundet svampeangreb, men traeets hovedstamme staar stadig tilbage' (was felled in 2018 due to fungal infection; only the main trunk stump remains). Never ship as a living entry. Recorded here so no future pass re-verifies it from the older, now-stale fredninger.dk description alone.

blocked.name: Bispebjerg Kirsebaeralle (Cherry Blossom Avenue), Bispebjerg Kirkegaard
blocked.species: Japanese flowering cherry (Prunus sp., likely Prunus serrulata / yedoensis cultivars)
blocked.reason: Genuinely famous (up to 150,000 visitors at peak bloom per tourism sources) and would be an easy sell, but it is a long avenue of many individual cherry trees along a cemetery path, not one collectible point or a compact famous ensemble with a single obvious place to stand; the trees themselves are also ordinary-aged flowering cherries (an ornamental planting), not ancient or individually remarkable specimens. Blocked under BRIEF_RESEARCH.md's explicit rule that 'an avenue or a whole wood is blocked', on the same logic as La Rambla's plane trees. Judged honestly per the brief's instruction, not defaulted.
